title: Python decompiler version coverage
subtitle: factual supported-version ranges across the CPython 3.x line
note: Bars show each tool's claimed CPython 3.x support, not accuracy. No competitor recovery percentage is plotted: disrobe cannot run these tools (no installs), so a head-to-head accuracy number would be fabricated. The honest, plottable difference is span. Axis is the CPython 3.x minor line where the active comparison lives; disrobe additionally disassembles 1.0-2.7 and 3.0-3.5 (legacy, partial), noted beside its bar. Versions encode as 3 + minor/100 (3.6 = 3.06, 3.15 = 3.15) so ordering is correct; labels render back to major.minor.

tools.name: pychd
tools.source: pychd README (github.com/diohabara/pychd): 3.0-3.14; 86.5% strict-AST / 43.2% behavioral are LLM-assisted and self-flagged likely-contaminated; deterministic mode emits pass-bodies

footnote: Deterministic tools reproduce identical output for identical input and cannot contaminate a benchmark. pychd is LLM-assisted and non-reproducible; its own README flags likely benchmark contamination, and its deterministic fallback leaves complex bodies as pass. disrobe is fully deterministic and reconstructs bodies.
